hint.label: Vocabulary

flip.text:
July 1997
The new Labour government publishes a White Paper (official government report) on devolution.

September 1997
Scotland and Wales hold referendums, both voting in favour of establishing assemblies in their countries.

1998
Introduction of Scotland Act 1998 and Government of Wales Bill.

Scotland Act and Government of Wales Bill

instruction.text: Click the buttons to read more about the corresponding events.

flip.text:
1972
On March 24, the British Government suspends the Stormont parliament due to ongoing conflicts and governs Northern Ireland centrally from London.

April 1998
The British and the Irish governments sign The Belfast/Good Friday Agreement, which declared that there would be a devolved Northern Irish government in the future.

instruction.text: Match each event with the corresponding date.
Click the buttons to read more about the corresponding events.

flip.text:
6 May 1999
Wales and Scotland hold elections to their respective Assemblies.

12 May 1999
First meeting of the Scottish Parliament in Edinburgh.

26 May 1999
The National Assembly for Wales is officially opened in Cardiff Bay, with the Queen in attendance at the ceremony.

1 July 1999
Devolution Day. The Scottish Parliament formally takes on its full authority with the Queen in attendance. The National Assembly for Wales is established, with powers previously held by the Secretary of State for Wales at Westminster being transferred to the new body

hint.label: Vocabulary

flip.text:
2000-2006
Devolution is suspended and restored on multiple occasions due to disagreements on issues like disarming weapons, until a procedure for decommissioning is agreed on in August 2001.

13 October 2006
British and Irish Governments present a plan to restore Northern Ireland's devolution.

1 December 2009
Northern Ireland Assembly passes a bill paving the way for devolution.

4 February 2010
Agreement on devolution is reached. Powers of policy and justice are passed from Westminster to Northern Ireland.

instruction.text: Match each event with the corresponding date.

atoms.a: Devolution remains unclear until procedure for decommis­sioning

instruction.text: Click the buttons to read more about the corresponding events.

flip.text:
March 2011
In a referendum, a majority of the Welsh electorate vote in favour of transferring additional legislative powers from the UK Parliament at Westminster to the Welsh Assembly.

18 September 2014
The Scottish Government holds a referendum on whether Scotland should become an independent state. The majority of Scotland votes to remain part of the United Kingdom.

2016
Brexit Referendum: In the United Kingdom European Union membership referendum, the majority of Britain votes to leave the European Union. However, the majority of Scotland Northern Ireland vote to remain in the EU.
